findings.sourceEvidence: SECTION 7.3 Limitation on Liens . Create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Lien upon any of its Property or revenues, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, except for: (a) Liens for taxes, assessments or charges not yet due or which are being contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings; provided that adequate reserves with respect thereto are maintained on the books of the Parent Borrower or its Subsidiaries, as the case may be, in conformity with GAAP;
findings.verifierReasoning: The source exception is a carve-out from a prohibition covering four modalities: create, incur, assume, and suffer to exist any Lien. The proposed IR expresses the exception only as a permission to CREATE_LIEN. It therefore omits the equally operative modalities 'incur', 'assume', and 'suffer to exist'. A statutory tax lien that attaches automatically to property, or a tax lien that the borrower assumes or passively suffers to remain, is excepted by the source when the stated conditions are met, but the proposed IR would not recognize that as a permitted lien because no lien is 'created'. This can change the compliance conclusion for a meaningful class of tax liens, so the discrepancy is material.

findings.sourceEvidence: SECTION 7.3 Limitation on Liens . Create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Lien upon any of its Property or revenues, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, except for: (a) Liens for taxes, assessments or charges not yet due or which are being contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings; provided that adequate reserves with respect thereto are maintained on the books of the Parent Borrower or its Subsidiaries, as the case may be, in conformity with GAAP;
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR does not state which entities may rely on the permission, nor that the permitted tax lien must be upon 'its Property or revenues' of the Parent Borrower or a Subsidiary. The reserve condition refers to the books of the Parent Borrower or its Subsidiaries, but the permission itself is not scoped to those entities or to Property/revenues in the entityScope fields. If the IR is consumed graph-wise, a tax lien of a Subsidiary, or a tax lien on revenues, may not be recognized as covered by the exception, or the permission may be read too broadly. Because 7.3(a) is a subclause of a larger section whose chapeau supplies this scope, and because the proposed IR is marked PARTIAL, I cannot be certain that this scope is not intended to be supplied by another rule; hence the severity is UNCERTAIN.
